title: `ps_create_time()` and `ps_boot_time()` drifts on Linux
description:
I noticed that `ps_create_time()` will return a different process creation time, depending on the creation time of the process that queries it.


First Process:
```bash
docker run -it --rm --name test rocker/r-ver:4.5.0
install.packages('ps')
Sys.getpid()
#> [1] 1
ps::ps_create_time(ps::ps_handle(1))
#> [1] "2025-05-07 17:50:18 GMT"
```

**_(wait a few minutes before launching second process)_**

Second Process:
```bash
docker exec -it test R
ps::ps_create_time(ps::ps_handle(1))
#> [1] "2025-05-07 17:50:35 GMT"
```

**_(wait a few more minutes)_**

Third Process:
```bash
docker exec -it test R
ps::ps_create_time(ps::ps_handle(1))
#> [1] "2025-05-07 17:51:00 GMT"
```

Document difference with `tasklist` on Windows
description:
I was trying to use ps to track down whether a particular system process was running on Windows or not. I found that I was able to do so by wrapping up `tasklist` with `shell()` but the process I was looking for didn't show up in `ps::ps()`. There are quite a few processes (at least on my machine) which behave similarly (see reprex below). I don't know that much about how system processes are categorised, it might be that there is a good reason for some to appear and not others. If that's the case, then I would suggest documenting what that difference is to avoid confusion.

``` r
library(ps)

nrow(read.csv(text = shell("tasklist /fo csv", intern = T)))
#> [1] 353
nrow(ps())
#> [1] 150
```

title: CleanupReporter() uses R6, rlang, and testthat without requireNamespace guards
description:
`CleanupReporter()` is an exported function that calls `R6::R6Class()`, `testthat::ProgressReporter`, `testthat::with_reporter()`, `testthat::quasi_label()`, `testthat::expect()`, and `rlang::enquo()` unconditionally. All three packages are declared as Suggests, not Imports.

Calling `ps::CleanupReporter()` without R6, rlang, or testthat installed produces a hard error with no informative message.

Wrapping the calls in `requireNamespace()` checks with an informative `stop()` if missing would fix this.

title: Possible PR: `ps_is_alive()`
description:
I'm adding a `ps_is_alive()` for my own package, and was wondering if you'd consider a PR here.

It caught me by surprise when `ps_is_running()` returned `FALSE` for a sleeping process on Linux. I know now that this is documented and expected behavior, but it still left me needing a way to determine if a process was in any of the alive states described by `ps_status()`.

```r
ps_is_alive <- function(p = ps_handle()) {
  assert_ps_handle(p)
  alive <- c("idle", "running", "sleeping", "disk_sleep", "uninterruptible", "waking")
  isTRUE(try(silent = TRUE, ps_status(p) %in% alive))
}
```

title: Convert to/from uid string
description:
I added a feature for my own use and was wondering if you'd like it for the repo.

```r
(p <- ps_handle())
#> <ps::ps_handle> PID=15544, NAME=rsession-utf8.exe, AT=2025-04-07 16:22:14.006244

(uid <- ps_to_uid(p))
#> [1] "1DY.KS0op03OU"

ps_from_uid(uid)
#> <ps::ps_handle> PID=15544, NAME=rsession-utf8.exe, AT=2025-04-07 16:22:14.006244
```

The uid is a base64 encoding of a process's pid and creation time. I found a string to be easier to transfer between processes and use for file/directory names.

I'd be happy to submit a pull request. Code is 100 lines, no extra dependencies. Just wanted to check first before adding documentation, tests, etc.

title: ps_environ() often has empty result on macOS
description:
The issue is that since Big Sur we cannot get the env vars of another process, most of the time. We can only get them if one of these conditions holds:

* kernel is DEVELOPMENT || DEBUG
* target process is same as current_proc()
* target process is not cs_restricted
* SIP is off
* caller has an entitlement

From https://github.com/apple/darwin-xnu/blob/2ff845c2e033bd0ff64b5b6aa6063a1f8f65aa32/bsd/kern/kern_sysctl.c#L1315-L1321

Seems like we can get it from an R process, even in RStudio where the exe of the main process is not the same as for the child process. I am not sure why.

There is not much we can do about this, but we need to document it, and it also affects process tree cleanup, here and in processx as well.

title: The `callr::r_session` process seems to hang on `Windows` after using `ps::ps_interrupt`
description:
### Brief Description

My sincere apologies if this issue doesn’t fit here, but I have run out of ideas of things to try.

In short:

- Executing the script `example.R` (i.e., see below) on `Windows` using `Rscript --vanilla example.R` causes it to return `NULL` instead of ``"Session `run` output.`` and then hang. Sometimes, the last `session$run` call is executed, but not always.
- If I place `Sys.sleep(0.1)` before the second-to-last `session$run`, the output seems to match what I would expect, but this feels arbitrary.
- The culprit seems to be `ps::ps_interrupt(p = handle, ctrl_c = TRUE)` because, after commenting it out, the script outputs as expected.

I would *greatly* appreciate your help in trying to understand what is happening...

```r
session <- callr::r_session$new()

# Create a cluster in the session.
invisible(session$run(function() {
    cluster <<- parallel::makeCluster(2, type = "PSOCK")
}))

# Get the worker PIDs.
worker_pids <- session$run(function() {
    parallel::clusterCall(cluster, Sys.getpid)
})

# Get handles to the worker processes.
worker_handles <- lapply(worker_pids, function(pid) {
    return(ps::ps_handle(pid))
})

# Keep the session busy (i.e., but not the workers.)
session$call(function() {
    while (TRUE) { Sys.sleep(0.1) }
})

# Allow some time for the call to kick in.
Sys.sleep(0.25)

# Get the state (i.e., expect `busy`).
cat(paste0("Session state before interrupt: ", session$get_state()), "\n\n")

# Interrupt the session.
session$interrupt()

# Get the state (i.e., expect `busy`).
cat(paste0("\nSession state after interrupt: ", session$get_state()), "\n\n")

# Wait for the session to be interrupted.
if (session$get_state() == "busy" && session$poll_process(0) == "timeout") {
    # Wait.
    session$poll_process(-1)
}

# Read the interrupt result (i.e., error).

})

# Verify that the workers are still alive.

    parallel::clusterEvalQ(cluster, {
        print(paste0("Worker `", Sys.getpid(), "` is alive."))
```

``` r
library(ps)

  os <- os[setdiff(names(os), c("BSD", "POSIX"))]
  names(os)[which(os)]
}


test_get_cpu_percs <- function() {
  # Get CPU times and record time
  initial_time <- Sys.time()
  initial_cpus <- ps_system_cpu_times()
  Sys.sleep(2)
  final_time <- Sys.time()
  final_cpus <- ps_system_cpu_times()
  
  # Difference in time
  delta_time <- as.numeric(initial_time - final_time, units = "secs")
  
  # Pre allocate percentages vector, and name
  cpu_percs <- vector(mode="numeric", length=length(initial_cpus))
  names(cpu_percs) <- names(initial_cpus)

  for (metric in names(initial_cpus)) {
    # CPU seconds
    delta_cpu <- initial_cpus[metric] - final_cpus[metric]
    # Divide CPU secs by time to get percentage, divide by no. CPUs
    # to ensure percentages are always below 100
    cpu_percs[metric] <- 100 * (delta_cpu / delta_time) / ps::ps_cpu_count()
    
    if (ps_os_name() != "WINDOWS") {
      # On linux divide by 100 to get to seconds from centiseconds
      print("Dividing...")
      cpu_percs[metric] <- cpu_percs[metric] / 100
    }
  }
  
  print(cpu_percs)
}
```

``` r
  Sys.sleep(2)
  final_time <- Sys.time()
  final_cpus <- ps_system_cpu_times()
  
  # Difference in time
  delta_time <- as.numeric(initial_time - final_time, units = "secs")
  
  # Pre allocate percentages vector, and name

  names(cpu_percs) <- names(initial_cpus)
  
  for (metric in names(initial_cpus)) {
    # CPU seconds
    delta_cpu <- initial_cpus[metric] - final_cpus[metric]
    # Divide CPU secs by time to get percentage, divide by no. CPUs
    # to ensure percentages are always below 100
    cpu_percs[metric] <- 100 * (delta_cpu / delta_time) / ps::ps_cpu_count()
    
    if (ps_os_name() != "WINDOWS") {
      # On linux divide by 100 to get to seconds from centiseconds
      print("Dividing...")
      cpu_percs[metric] <- cpu_percs[metric] / 100
    }
  }
```

description:
The ps_memory_info() on Linux reports memory size in pages and on windows in bytes. This is inconsistent. It would be great if memory sizes were reported in bytes on all OSs, as it is in Python's psutils.

https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc.5.html
```
/proc/[pid]/statm
              Provides information about memory usage, measured in
              pages.
```

In Python psutils it is multiplied by PAGESIZE
https://github.com/giampaolo/psutil/blob/c687f99789d8bdd7efa0b9b4787ae67cf184884b/psutil/_pslinux.py#L1897
```python
        with open_binary("%s/%s/statm" % (self._procfs_path, self.pid)) as f:
            vms, rss, shared, text, lib, data, dirty = \
                [int(x) * PAGESIZE for x in f.readline().split()[:7]]
```

In R ps it is used as is:
https://github.com/r-lib/ps/blob/603d3b3a9baec7eed6cc27b2f6ec9d034edf6461/src/api-linux.c#L770
```c
 ret = snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "/proc/%d/statm", handle->pid);
 ...
 ret = ps__read_file(path, &buf, /* buffer= */ 1024);
 ...
 ret = sscanf(buf, "%lu %lu %lu %lu %lu %lu %lu", &rss, &vms, &shared,
	       &text, &lib, &data, &dirty);
 ...
  PROTECT(result = allocVector(INTSXP, 7));
  INTEGER(result)[0] = rss;
  INTEGER(result)[1] = vms;
```

title: ld: library not found for -lomp
description:
Hi, as has been reported a number of times (#56, #81, #108), `ps` has issues if you use a non-standard compiler on OSX: ``` installing *source* package ‘ps’ ... ** package ‘ps’ successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked ** using staged installation ** libs /opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang -fopenmp -g -O3 -Wall -pedantic -std=gnu99 -mtune=native -pipe -Wall px.c -o px ld: library not found for -lomp clang-11: error: linker command failed with exit code 1 (use -v to see invocation) make: *** [px] Error 1 ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘ps’ * removing ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.1-arm64/Resources/library/ps’ Error in i.p(...) : (converted from warning) installation of package ‘ps’ had non-zero exit status ``` The problem is that you don't add the linker flags in [src/Makevars.in]: What it looks like: ``` px: px.c $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Wall px.c -o px interrupt: interrupt.c $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Wall interrupt.c -o interrupt ``` The fix: 
px: px.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Wall px.c -o px $(LDFLAGS)

interrupt: interrupt.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Wall interrupt.c -o interrupt $(LDFLAGS)
Note: I'm anything but a C crack, you probably should ask someone with a deeper understanding of `Makefile` syntax whether there are any unintended side-effects. But it works for me™ Best regards, Stefan

```r
library(processx)

p <- process$new("bash", c("-c", "sleep 100"))
ps <- p$as_ps_handle()
print(ps::ps_name(ps))
```

After some testing, I believe the problem is that `PS__CHECK_STAT` does strict equality checks against doubles. I am testing a patch and will open a PR shortly.

title: `r-lib/setup-r-depdencies` needs to be updated in order to avoid pak failure in GA runs.
description:
Because of a change in Ubuntu; switching to `sudo -rs`, passing `-E` to `sudo` causes an error downstream because `Sys.getenv()` will return an empty string for `pak` to be installed in. Causing github actions runs to fail very early. 

```
Run # Install pak
Install pak
    sudo: preserving the entire environment is not supported, '-E' is ignored
    > dir.create(Sys.getenv("R_LIB_FOR_PAK"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    Error in dir.create(Sys.getenv("R_LIB_FOR_PAK"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) : 
      zero-length 'path' argument
    Execution halted

```

This was fixed in `setup-r-dependencies` v2.13.0. : https://github.com/r-lib/actions/pull/1096

As long as this is not fixed, any github actions workflow using setup-r-dependencies will fail early. 

Example of run on ps: https://github.com/PietrH/ps/actions/runs/42847194024
